Call `peter()` without a prompt from an interactive R console to chat. It uses your current
environment and the configured model. Choose a route explicitly with
`peter(model = "openai/gpt-6-sol")`. [Language models](language-models.html) covers API, CLI
and local setup.

On a new console with no explicit or configured model, Peter first offers the Codex CLI, the
Claude Code CLI and manual API/Ollama setup. Selecting an installed CLI that reports
`Signed in` saves its default model in your user settings and opens the console. `Unknown`
permits your explicit choice with a notice; `Not signed in` returns to R with terminal sign-in
instructions. CLI-reported login does not verify online access or subscription billing; an
API-key login can also count as signed in. Context-sharing acknowledgment remains separate.

Manual setup prints API and local Ollama commands and returns to R; cancellation (choose Cancel
or press Enter), a missing CLI or a non-CLI replacement of a shortcut also returns without saving
a default. Configure a model as shown in [Language models](language-models.html), then call
`peter()` again.
An existing session, an explicit or effective configured model, `.stdin = TRUE` and
noninteractive workflows skip setup. Calls with a prompt use their normal model resolution.

The saved default applies in future R sessions and projects unless a higher-priority setting
overrides it. Use `gptr_config(model = "provider/model", .scope = "user")` to change it; see
[Configuration](configuration.html) for precedence and settings locations.


``` r
library(gptr)
session = peter()
# At peter>, enter: Plot mpg against wt in mtcars.
# Then enter: /exit
```

The default prompt is `peter> `; other permission modes appear as `peter[plan]> `,
`peter[edits]> ` or `peter[auto]> `. Enter `/exit` to return the session invisibly to `session`.
Objects created by the agent remain in the environment where the console runs.
R tools compute on those in-memory objects across turns; you can inspect or reuse them at the
R prompt without exporting and reloading a dataset. Model context is a separate, bounded
description of that workspace; see [Execution model](execution-model.html) for copying and
storage.

For input piped to an R process, `peter(.stdin = TRUE)` explicitly reads standard input using
the same syntax; end of input returns the session. The console UI can consume permission
answers from that input too. Configure the model, credentials and permissions before
unattended work.

For programmatic event streams, select `.opts = list(frontend = "jsonl")`. With `.stdin = TRUE`,
that frontend treats every input line as a literal model prompt (or a JSON prompt record);
`/exit` and `/quit` end the stream. Slash commands and `!` execution use the console frontend.
JSONL stdout contains event records, with human-readable notices on stderr.

Continue the same session from R:


``` r
session |> peter()
# At peter>, enter: Explain the pattern in that plot.
# Then enter: /exit
```

Piping uses the session's kept workspace. To explore independently, use
`gptr_fork(session) |> peter()`; writes stay in the fork's overlay. `/clear` resets the
conversation while retaining workspace objects, model and mode.

## Enter prompts, objects and your own R

Ask in ordinary language. `@x` attaches a visible R object by name, and `@analysis.R` adds the
beginning of a text file. Quote a path containing spaces as `@"analysis notes.txt"`.
Files take precedence when a mention matches both a file and an object. A file mention sends
at most its first 40 lines; binary files contribute a description rather than their contents.
For a larger file, ask the agent to read the relevant section.

```text
peter> Compare @mtcars columns mpg and wt.
peter> Explain the approach in @analysis.R.
peter> !head(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt")])
peter> Now suggest a diagnostic plot.
```

`!code` runs your R code immediately in the console environment, prints its output and adds
a compact note of the code and output to the **next** model prompt. It does not send a prompt
or spend model tokens by itself. The note is bounded to about 300 estimated tokens, so inspect
large results in R and send the part the model needs.

`!!code` also runs immediately, but does not add that code/output note. Changes it makes are
still part of the workspace that later calls can inspect or describe. Neither prefix passes
through the model's permission gate: you are explicitly running your own R code. Do not paste
unreviewed code merely because the agent suggested it.

In terminal R with readline, R in an IDE's Terminal tab included, Tab completes R names and
file paths after `!` and `!!`. RStudio's console completes R code at `peter>` too; radian and
Positron's console offer no completion there.

```text
peter> !fit = lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
peter> !coef(fit)
peter> Explain the slope I just fitted.
peter> !!local_note = "Check the measurement units later"
```

For multiple lines, use a triple-quoted prompt, a trailing backslash to continue a prompt, or
a fenced R block. A fence marked `r`, `R`, `{r}` or unmarked behaves like `!code`; any other
fence, such as one marked `python`, is sent as prompt text. Incomplete `!`/`!!` R expressions
continue at the `+ ` prompt until they parse. Very long single lines can exceed R's console
input limit; use an `@file` or a multiline prompt instead.

In CRAN's R for macOS in a terminal a pasted block is one input: its lines join the first one
and `... ` waits for Enter, where text you type is added. A pasted fence or `"""` block is read up
to its closer at once, and a block pasted at an approval or a choice is kept in the console
history and the question asked again. A last pasted line without a newline waits for Enter at
the next prompt, so a two-line paste without a final newline answers with its first line.
Homebrew or conda R, Linux terminals, RStudio, R.app, Positron and Windows deliver pasted lines
one at a time, so wrap a multi-line paste in `"""` there. Lines typed, pasted or run from a
script before a question appears (an approval, a choice, the pause menu) never answer it: while
an answer runs they are queued for the agent as `type_ahead` says (a `/command` or `!code` line
waits for the next prompt), otherwise they go to the console history. Answer after the prompt.

```text
peter> """
... Fit mpg on wt.
... Explain the units and give one diagnostic.
... """
```

```text
peter> ```r
... fit = lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
... coef(fit)
... ```
```

These input forms apply inside Peter's chat; at the ordinary R prompt, use normal R syntax.
Console inputs may enter R's history (`gptr.history`), and an enabled transcript can record
user-run code. `!!` is a control over the next prompt note, not a privacy boundary.

## Commands

These are all built-in slash commands. Arguments in brackets are optional. `/help` lists the
commands available in the current session, including any supplied by plugins or prompt templates.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/help [command]` | List input syntax and commands, or describe one command. |
| `/exit`, `/quit`, `/q` | Leave the chat and return its session. |
| `/model [provider/model or alias]` | Show the model or switch it from the next request; keeps the conversation. |
| `/mode [plan|manual|edits|auto|yolo]` | Show the mode or switch it from the next turn. |
| `/plan` | Switch to plan mode for read-only exploration and a proposed plan. |
| `/tools` | List direct tools and `peter$` members. |
| `/env [pattern]` | Describe workspace objects whose names contain the pattern. |
| `/compact [focus]` | Compact the conversation now, optionally emphasizing a topic; may make a model request. |
| `/cost` | Show this session's tokens and cost. |
| `/context` | Show the token ledger of the last request. |
| `/status` | Show session, model, mode, document and queued messages. |
| `/clear` | Start a new conversation while retaining workspace objects, model and mode. |
| `/resume [id]` | List stored sessions or continue the selected session in this console. |
| `/fork` | Continue on a new session with an overlay workspace. |
| `/doc [path]` | Show the recording document or bind one; binding authorizes writes to it. |
| `/skills` | List discoverable skills. |
| `/skill:<name> [request]` | Preload a skill and send the request; without a request, ask the agent to use that skill. |
| `/mcp` | List MCP servers. |
| `/permissions` | Show the permission rules. |
| `/permissions allow|ask|deny|remove <rule>` | Change a rule for this R process, for example `/permissions allow r(fn:saveRDS)`. |
| `/retry` | Undo the last turn and send its recovered prompt again; may make a model request. |
| `/undo` | Undo the last turn's restorable objects, files and conversation. |
| `/redo` | Redo what the last rewind undid. |
| `/rewind [k]` | Offer a rewind menu, or retain turns 1 through `k`. |
| `/checkpoints [all]` | List current checkpoints, or all branches when `all` is given. |

Undo and rewind report partial restores when something cannot be captured or restored. External
side effects are not generally reversible. See `?gptr_rewind` and `?gptr_security` before relying
on restoration.

## Approve, interrupt and continue

In `manual`, known read-only actions and actions covered by existing allow rules run directly;
other changes ask for approval under the call they gate, and you type the answer on the row
below. The question lists the flagged calls, riskiest first (at most five; `?` shows all), and
offers `y` for this action, `a` for a session rule covering them when one can be written (`p` for
the same rule in this project), `n` to deny, and `?` for details. A sub-agent's question names
it (`? sub-agent A: allow r?`); an answer that is none of these is explained, and five such answers
refuse the action. `edits` allows project file edits
while still asking about R changes unless an allow rule applies; `auto` allows ordinary actions
while retaining critical and secret guards. `plan` offers read-only tools and level-1 R
exploration in a scratch environment, where intermediate bindings can change while the user
workspace is preserved. Settings and policies are described in
[Configuration](configuration.html) and `?gptr_security`.

In a terminal (terminal R or an IDE's Terminal tab; not Windows), a line you type while an
answer runs steers it: the agent reads it at its next step, after the current tool results.
gptr shows it on a dim line that names its kind (`steer`), then as your own line, at column 0,
when the agent reads it. Lines typed or pasted together are one message. The terminal does not
echo while an answer runs: a typed line shows after Enter, on its dim line, and never mixes into
the answer.
With `gptr_config(type_ahead = "follow_up", .scope = "user")` each is a follow-up instead: the
next prompt, sent once the answer ends. `/commands` and `!code` typed during an answer also run
at the next prompt, in the order typed. A steer the answer did not take (it ended first) is the
next prompt too; after an interrupt or an error nothing you queued is sent: it goes to the
console history, and Up recalls it. On the CLI routes (`claude-cli`, `codex`) a steer reaches the model
after the CLI's current response. The RStudio, Positron and R.app consoles hold typed input
until R reads again, so there a line typed during an answer becomes the next prompt;
type-ahead during `peter("...")` at R's prompt stays R's next input.

While an answer or tool runs in a supported terminal, Ctrl-C opens a pause menu:

- **Steer** delivers a new instruction after the current tool results.
- **Follow-up** queues a prompt: in the chat it is the next prompt, sent once the answer ends;
  in a `peter("...")` call it is sent when the agent would otherwise stop. In the chat a
  `/command` or `!code` line typed at Steer or Follow-up runs at the next prompt.
- **Continue** resumes the current work.
- **Abort** stops it and retains the partial session; what you queued goes to the history, unsent.

A foreground call, including a chat turn, can also offer **background** when that experimental
capability is available. It returns to `peter>` while the run remains active. Another prompt
steers the running session; `!!gptr::gptr_wait(gptr::gptr_last())` waits for completion without
adding a code/output note to the next prompt. Returning to the chat prompt does not guarantee
progress while it waits for input. Under Rscript, background runs advance only inside blocking
gptr calls. Inline R tools still occupy the same R process while they execute.

At the chat prompt, one interrupt prints a hint; two consecutive interrupts leave the chat.
Use Ctrl-C in a terminal, an IDE's Terminal tab included, and in Positron's console, and the
front end's interrupt key in other IDE consoles: Esc in RStudio, R.app and RGui. IDEs that cannot resume an
interrupted evaluation use an abort fallback; pause/resume behavior is not uniformly verified
across front ends.

The equivalent session verbs work from R:


``` r
gptr_steer(session, "Use the existing fit instead of fitting again.")
gptr_steer(session, "Summarize the diagnostics at the end.", as = "follow_up")
gptr_wait(session)
gptr_cancel(session)
```

For persistent conversation storage, initialize a project with `gptr_init(path)` and review its
trust decision. `gptr_sessions()` lists stored sessions, and `gptr_resume(id)` recovers one.
[Script as history](script-as-history.html) covers document recording, replay and
transcripts; [Language models](language-models.html) covers scripted calls that need no
interactive console.
